clue.text: Careless about young lady

parts.note: re is the Latin-derived word for about or concerning
miss is a title for a young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: Someone is accused of being careless around a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Being negligent in one's duties is to be slack, inattentive and careless.

clue.text: Speak out, upsetting church in solemn observance

indicators.note: in places the church piece inside the observance

parts.note: a rite is a solemn ceremony or observance

indicators.note: in a down answer, upsetting turns the church letters upside down, reading upward

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone protests about a church being disrupted during a sacred ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'upsetting' flips the church letters to read upward, and 'in' sets them within the ceremony; 'Speak out' is the definition, not 'solemn observance'.
explanation.definitionFit: To declaim or say aloud from memory is to speak out.

clue.text: Mischance disorganised skilled workers

indicators.note: disorganised means put into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mishap throws the tradesmen into confusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Engineers and repairers who maintain machinery are skilled workers.

clue.text: It incorporates elements of unceremonious language

definitions.text: It incorporates elements of unceremonious language

indicators.note: incorporating elements of a phrase means holding a run of its letters, so the answer is hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A description of casual speech borrowing bits of informal talk.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'It incorporates' cannot stand for the answer; the whole clue both hides the letters and describes informal speech, so it is an all-in-one.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal, casual vocabulary is speech without ceremony.

clue.text: Put forward as Brit against euro?

definitions.meaning: to put forward an idea or theory for consideration
a Briton who opposed the euro would favour sterling, being pro the pound

explanation.surface: A British politician puts forward a case against the single currency.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into PRO (for) and POUND (sterling): a Briton against the euro is for the pound.
explanation.definitionFit: To advance a theory or proposal for others to consider is to offer it up.

clue.text: Quick foray gets pawn captured

indicators.note: captured says the pawn is held inside the foray

parts.note: a raid is a sudden foray or attack
P is the chess abbreviation for pawn

explanation.surface: A swift attack results in a chess pawn being taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Swift and fast are synonyms of quick.

clue.text: Normal sum for chief

parts.note: par is the normal or expected standard
an amount is a sum, as of money

explanation.surface: An ordinary total for a leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Supreme or foremost in importance is chief.

clue.text: Subject to articles of European Union

parts.note: un is a French indefinite article and der a German definite article, two European languages' articles
un is a French indefinite article and der a German definite article, two European languages' articles

explanation.surface: Bound by the treaty articles of the European Union.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'articles' are grammatical words in French and German, not clauses of a treaty.
explanation.definitionFit: Being beneath or governed by a rule means being subject to it.

clue.text: Alter the form of false teeth, eating article

indicators.note: eating says the article is swallowed inside the false teeth

parts.note: a denture is a set of false teeth
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Dentures chewing an item get bent out of shape.
explanation.definitionFit: To change something's natural character or nature is to alter its form.

clue.text: In short time, that is producing rust, possibly

definitions.text: In short time, that is producing rust, possibly

indicators.note: In at the front says the rearranged letters go inside the following pieces

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a brief time
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of rust may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Something that, given a little while, can cause corrosion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' shuffles the rust letters and 'In' sets them between the I and E; read whole, the clue also describes damp, which corrodes iron in a short while.
explanation.definitionFit: Dampness or wetness in the air causes iron to corrode.

clue.text: Exultant fellow fronting a band

indicators.note: fronting says the first piece stands before the pieces that follow it

parts.note: cock is an old familiar term of address for a man or chap
a hoop is a circular band, as round a barrel

explanation.surface: A jubilant man has become the frontman of a music group.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone crowing with triumph is jubilant, elated and exultant.

clue.text: Art master at home on the staff

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece written on another follows it

parts.note: a rod is a stick or staff
in means at home, as in 'staying in tonight'

explanation.surface: A great painter is living at home while employed on the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: Auguste Rodin was the French sculptor of The Thinker, so 'Art master' is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: The French sculptor was a master of his art, one of the great names of modern sculpture.

clue.text: Idle chatter after race that irritates viewers

indicators.note: after places the chatter piece behind the race piece

parts.note: to tear is to rush or race along
gas is informal for idle talk or chatter

explanation.surface: Pointless commentary following a race annoys the television audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'viewers' are eyes, which is what the riot-control spray irritates; the definition reads as a noun phrase, the thing that irritates eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: This riot-control spray stings the eyes, the body's own viewers, making them stream.

clue.text: Fault in red item that needs fixing

indicators.note: something that needs fixing is broken and must be put back together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A defect has been found in a red object that requires repair.
explanation.definitionFit: A black mark or failing counted against someone is a fault.

clue.text: Sound in heart and not complaining

definitions.meaning: a healthy heart beats with no abnormal noise detected by a stethoscope
accepting something silently, with no grumble or protest

explanation.surface: A patient takes the doctor's verdict on their heart without protest.
explanation.walkthrough: A heart murmur is an extra sound heard through a stethoscope, so a heart that is sound lacks one.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes uncomplaining acceptance, and literally a heart with no abnormal sound.

clue.text: Groupies taking heroin make boy very cross

parts.note: H is slang for heroin
anger is the state of being very cross, and to anger is to make someone so; 'make' is link wording
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: Fans on drugs infuriate a young lad.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers who attach themselves to a celebrity are hangers-on, or groupies.

clue.text: Evening fun provided by a squeeze and kiss? Not half!

parts.note: to press is to squeeze

indicators.note: not half means only half of the word kiss is used, its first two letters

explanation.surface: A hug and a kiss supply the evening's entertainment, and how!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is also British slang for 'and how!', disguising the instruction to take half of 'kiss'. The answer is the social life after a day's skiing.
explanation.definitionFit: Socialising at a resort after a day on the slopes is evening entertainment.

clue.text: Doctor altered doses in case of intermittent depression

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor

indicators.note: altered means changed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A physician changed the dosage for a patient with recurring low moods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' is link wording; the doctor's MO is followed by ODINESS, the rearranged DOSES IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluctuating gloom or sulkiness that comes and goes is a changeable temperament.

clue.text: Final bit of work a theologian gets to finish with hesitation

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian
end means to finish
um is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A theologian completes his final piece of writing, hesitantly.
explanation.definitionFit: An appendix or supplement added at the close of a book is its final bit.

clue.text: One gets terrible indigestion eating animal in state of decay

indicators.note: eating says the animal is swallowed inside the rearranged letters
terrible says the letters of indigestion are in a dreadful jumbled state

parts.note: a rat is an animal

explanation.surface: Someone suffers awful indigestion after eating some creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One gets' is link wording, not the letter I: 'terrible' jumbles indigestion and 'eating' sets the rodent after its G.
explanation.definitionFit: Crumbling and falling apart is decay, the breaking up of something into fragments.

clue.text: Man meeting an academic in direct confrontation

parts.note: he is a man, the male pronoun
an is the indefinite article, a
a don is a university academic

explanation.surface: A man has a face-to-face clash with a university lecturer.
explanation.definitionFit: Facing directly, front to front, describes a direct confrontation or collision.

clue.text: A gun grabbed by journalist in London area

indicators.note: grabbed by says the gun and A are held inside the journalist

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist
the Sten is a British submachine gun

explanation.surface: A reporter seizes a firearm in part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is the traditionally working-class area of east London.
explanation.definitionFit: This district east of the City is a well-known part of the capital.

clue.text: Fire projectiles at boat

definitions.meaning: a light, narrow racing rowing boat

explanation.definitionFit: To bombard with artillery, and also a light racing rowing boat.

clue.text: Look for water and plunge into it

definitions.meaning: to search for underground water with a divining rod
to drench or immerse in water, a variant spelling of douse

explanation.definitionFit: Divining for underground springs with a rod, and also drenching or immersing.

clue.text: Fruitless steps to restrict monarch

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so the monarch is held inside the steps

parts.note: a stile is a set of steps for climbing over a fence
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Attempts to curb a king's power prove useless.
explanation.definitionFit: Barren, unproductive and bearing no fruit all mean fruitless.

clue.text: The Continental female, fashionable and dainty

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the, a Continental the
in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'

explanation.surface: A stylish European woman is delicate.
explanation.definitionFit: Small, delicate and fairy-like describes something dainty.

clue.text: Compulsion to chuck out superior attire

indicators.note: to chuck out is to throw away, so a letter is removed

parts.note: duress is compulsion by threat or force
U stands for upper-class or superior, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: Someone is forced to discard their best clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing or a garment worn is one's attire.

clue.text: Place with well-known vicar to animate part of the country.

parts.note: to wake is to rouse or bring to life
a field is a piece of countryside

explanation.surface: A town with a famous clergyman seeks to enliven its rural region.
explanation.walkthrough: Goldsmith's novel The Vicar of Wakefield makes this Yorkshire town the place with a famous vicar.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yorkshire city is the setting named in Goldsmith's novel about a country clergyman.

clue.text: Mother, idle, to stay in bed for no good reason?

definitions.text: to stay in bed for no good reason?

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
to linger is to idle or dawdle

explanation.surface: A mother is lazy, staying in bed without any excuse.
explanation.definitionFit: To feign illness to avoid work, as by lying in bed, is to shirk.

clue.text: Agreement boy should be accepted by Cambridge, say

indicators.note: a boy accepted by a university joins it, so the son piece is attached to the university piece

parts.note: Cambridge is an example of a university, uni for short
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: Agreement that a lad ought to get a place at Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in concert or harmony is being in accord or agreement.
